_comment: Reviewed verification recipes for scripts/register-secret-verified.sh --recipe <name> (claude-code-skills#478). A recipe lands only by PR, with the provider's documented behaviour cited in its evidence field. Network recipes must carry a negative control: the same request with a wrong value must answer differently, or nothing is stored. Behaviour that can only be measured with a real value (the provider's answer to a wrong client secret) is measured by that control on every run, and the first real run's answers are the ledger row's detail. Never add a recipe that stores without a check.

access-service-token.evidence: Cloudflare Rotate a service token API: POST accounts/{account_id}/access/service_tokens/{service_token_id}/rotate. previous_client_secret_expires_at is explicit because omission expires the old secret immediately. Preserve its original expires_at until Router release smoke. The existing token, reusable Service Auth policy and four-destination application were read back from the company account on 2026-11-01. On 2026-11-02 the owner confirmed Mac Studio was returned; retirement of f and the retained a/b/c topology must be read back before registration. Every run rechecks the full application inventory and policies, then requires three HTTP403 wrong-secret controls and three HTTP200 OpenAI models JSON responses without redirects. https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/zero_trust/subresources/access/subresources/service_tokens/methods/rotate/

access-service-token-recovery.evidence: Recover only the same pair retained by the reviewed rotation recipe after a refused probe or partial GitHub registration. Never POST or rotate. Bind the owner-only saved result and required timestamps to the current service-token metadata and preserved original expiry, then repeat the complete three-origin configuration, retired-f absence and negative-control/real JSON checks before the existing store. The original recovery remains untouched until audited GitHub readback. https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/zero_trust/subresources/access/subresources/service_tokens/methods/rotate/

github-oauth.evidence: GitHub REST 2022-11-28, Check a token: Basic auth with client_id / client_secret; 'Invalid tokens will return 404 NOT FOUND'. The control counts only a definite authentication failure, 401, as 'the endpoint told the wrong secret apart'. GitHub does not document the answer to a wrong client secret (only 200 / 404 / 422 are listed), so a first run that answers anything else refuses and is itself the measurement (M1). No answer, 403, 429, 5xx or a non-JSON body is inconclusive for both requests.

slack-oauth.evidence: https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/oauth.v2.access/ documents Basic auth, invalid_code (the code is invalid), bad_client_secret (the client_secret is invalid), and checking ok on every response. Accept only HTTP 200 with ok=false on both requests and exactly the named errors. This is a comparative probe, not a documented guarantee that invalid_code authenticates the pair: Slack does not document check order. M2 on 2026-11-01 returned real status=200 error=invalid_code; control status=200 error=invalid_code, so this probe cannot verify that pair and must refuse. Never accept invalid_code as a successful control or store the pair without a discriminating check. No answer, 403, 429, 5xx or a non-JSON body is inconclusive for both requests; any other unmatched response also refuses.

mcp-token.evidence: cor-os packages/computer-mcp/src/index.ts authorize(): 'Bearer <MCP_TOKEN>' is compared exactly, so no provider can verify it; release-secrets.mjs boundedSecret: at most 256 KiB. packages/computer-mcp/README.md: the administrator's UAT uses the MCP Bearer, so the value is also kept in Bitwarden (the env ledger), never shown.

intake-keys.evidence: cor-os docs/publishing-corpus.md:134-141 and release-secrets.mjs validatePublishingIntakeKeys: 4 distinct 32-byte keys plus revisions in canonical order. The generator and the check are the consumer's own commands (cor-os#126); until cor-os has them the recipe refuses.

slack-oauth-code.evidence: https://docs.slack.dev/authentication/installing-with-oauth/ documents state and a ten-minute authorization code; https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/oauth.v2.access/ documents Basic client authentication and successful token exchange. First require HTTP 200 ok:false bad_client_secret with the same valid code and a wrong secret, then HTTP 200 ok:true with the real pair. Check the exact app, team, pre-approved user and users:read-only user grant. https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/auth.revoke/ documents ok:true revoked:true; require this for every received token before GitHub storage. No real code flow measured yet. A consumed code or non-discriminating control refuses. A new grant and a separate execution approval are operator preconditions; no cor-os login or production route is used.
